headlines.title: Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days: Shares surge 30%
headlines.summary:
Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi breaks down the stunning news of the morning: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstating founder Jensen Huang as CEO just 12 days after his resignation. Including his five takeaways on what the reversal says about corporate governance, the role Washington played in the decision, and the rally that's lifting the whole AI trade while sending AMD lower.

Brian is joined by New Street Research technology infrastructure analyst Antoine Chkaiban on the new checks around Huang and why he's still a buyer; "In the Loop" host Ejaz on key-man risk and whether the "Bank of Nvidia" reopens for neoclouds; EMJ Capital founder and president Eric Jackson, who calls the return a win for open-source AI; Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman on the board's credibility and Colette Kress's future; Moor Insights & Strategy founder and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead on the politics behind the ouster and why nothing changes for AMD for 18 months; and SlateStone Wealth partner and chief market strategist Kenny Polcari on whether this kicks off a year-end rally.

news.summary: Sandisk shares rose sharply on Monday as part of a broad AI and tech rebound, according to a TIKR note that says the stock jumped far more than Meta (up 6%) and Cipher (up 17%). The rally followed Nvidia's board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. Simply Wall St separately reports the stock returned 179% over the past year and has since pulled back steeply.

headlines.title: Semiconductor Stocks like Micron, Marvell, and Bloom Energy See Massive Gains as Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA
headlines.summary:
Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%.

Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves.

Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.

headlines.summary:
Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA is lifting technology stocks on Monday. The NASDAQ was up more than 7% as of 1:30 p.m. Eastern, after opening with a 3% pre-market gain following Friday's sell-off. Chip stocks as a group rose more than 13%.

Software is also higher, but the gains are uneven. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) are each up about 3%, while the IGV software ETF is up 4%. The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.

Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.
